$comment: World Bank indicators rendered by the Economy tab. Unit and basis live here rather than at the call site, because a monetary figure without a currency and a current/constant designation is not a fact — 'GDP: 29,184,890,000,000' is unusable and 'GDP grew 8%' is meaningless without knowing whether the series is nominal or real. The Fact for every monetary indicator is built from this table, so a missing unit is a build-time gap rather than a rendering omission.

basisValues.current-usd: Current US dollars. Not adjusted for inflation; year-on-year changes mix real growth with price changes and exchange-rate movement.
basisValues.constant-usd: Constant US dollars at a fixed base year. Inflation-adjusted, so changes are real.
basisValues.ppp: Purchasing power parity international dollars. A modelled conversion, inherently approximate.
basisValues.local-current: Current local currency units. Not comparable across countries, and broken across a redenomination.
basisValues.ratio: A percentage or index. No currency applies.
basisValues.count: A count of people or units. No currency applies.

indicators.name: GDP (PPP)
indicators.note: PPP conversion factors are modelled, so this is an estimate rather than a reported figure.

indicators.name: Real GDP growth
indicators.note: Can be negative, so a logarithmic scale is not available for this series.

indicators.name: Inflation, consumer prices
indicators.note: Can be negative during deflation, so a logarithmic scale is not available.

indicators.name: Unemployment
indicators.note: ILO modelled estimate for most countries rather than a national reported figure.

indicators.name: Gini index
indicators.note: Published only in survey years, so gaps are normal and expected.
